docs.title: Aware
docs.text:
Aware is a V3 Assess prototype for telemetry-based root-cause analysis. It combines a Parser agent, an Executor agent, and dynamic analysis sub-agents to identify an incident's root-cause component, occurrence time, and reason.

Both the aware CLI and the web UI can analyze one incident or a dataset batch. Nezha and OpenRCA Bank, Market, and Telecom batches use the same dataset catalogue preparation. The CLI batch command needs a dataset name and an extracted source directory; AWARE generates each incident request automatically.

The project focuses on a clear runtime flow:

  • prepare dataset incidents or parse a free-form request into a BuildSpec
  • select the relevant telemetry files
  • run specialized log, trace, and metrics agents under a per-incident agent limit
  • filter analysis on failure_time_range_ts
  • report the selected root cause and a causal evidence graph
  • persist batch scores, journals, JSON/text reports, graphs, and optional SQLite memory

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text: Interface Use it for CLI Running dataset batches or parser-only, executor-only, and single-incident assessments. Web UI Running dataset batches or single incidents while inspecting live events and results.

docs.title: Core Components
docs.text: Component Role ParserAgent Converts a user incident request into a validated BuildSpec. ExecutorAgent Instantiates analysis sub-agents and coordinates execution. tools/ Provides file loading, time-window filtering, and telemetry helpers. templates/ Defines dynamic agent templates for logs, traces, and metrics. Knowledge DB Stores runs, events, task results, and findings in a per-run SQLite file when memory is enabled.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Install and configure Aware
  • Run the CLI commands
  • Use the web UI
  • Review the runtime architecture

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Aware is organized around a V3 agent runtime with explicit boundaries between dataset preparation, parsing, execution, tools, templates, and persistence. The UI and CLI share the same dataset catalogue builders and source-directory resolver.

docs.title: Runtime Flow
docs.text:
Dataset + extracted source -> Nezha/OpenRCA catalogue -> incident request
Single incident question -----------------------------> incident request
Incident request -> ParserAgent
  -> BuildSpec
  -> ExecutorAgent
  -> Metrics, logs, traces, and focused V3 sub-agents
  -> Findings, root-cause synthesis, and causal graph
  -> Scores, reports, journals, and optional SQLite memory

docs.title: Parser Agent
docs.text:
ParserAgent converts an incident request into a BuildSpec. Canonical Nezha and OpenRCA batch incidents take a deterministic, validated parser path; free-form questions use the retrying LLM parser. It loads BuildSpec rules from:

knowledge/parser_buildspec_kb.md

The knowledge file contains:

  • task_1..task_7 mapping
  • BuildSpec contract
  • normalization rules
  • file selection rules for logs, traces, and metrics

docs.title: Executor Agent
docs.text:
ExecutorAgent instantiates sub-agents from templates and coordinates their analysis against selected telemetry files. The metrics, logs, and traces domains run as needed; V3 specialists and focused follow-ups can investigate unresolved evidence. EXECUTOR_MAX_AGENTS is a ceiling on all agents created per incident, including those follow-ups. It is not a concurrency setting.

Implementation:

agents/executor_agent.py

Executor knowledge is loaded from:

knowledge/executor_rca_v3_kb.md

docs.title: Dynamic Agent Templates
docs.text:
Executor sub-agents are defined in:

templates/assess_templates.py

Each template defines:

  • agent_name
  • role
  • objective
  • BuildSpec target_field
  • tools to use
  • telemetry domain

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Telemetry helpers live in:

tools/telemetry_tools.py

Examples:

  • load_csv_window
  • build_llm_observation_context
  • count_matches
  • sample_matching_lines
  • max_numeric_column

These helpers keep data access and time-window filtering outside of agent orchestration.

docs.title: Batch persistence
docs.text: By default, each CLI or UI batch gets a UTC timestamped directory under output/batches/<batch-id>/. It contains problems.csv, config.json, results.csv, per-incident journals and reports, and graph PNGs when a causal graph is produced. With memory enabled, each incident gets its own SQLite file under memory/. See Outputs for the full layout.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Aware reads configuration from environment variables and optional CLI parameters. The same provider and runtime settings apply to dataset batches in the CLI and UI.

docs.title: LLM Provider
docs.text:
Aware supports OpenAI-compatible APIs and Ollama Cloud. Select the provider with AWARE_LLM_PROVIDER (openai-compatible by default, or ollama). The ollama value selects the cloud endpoint, not a local Ollama process. ollama-cloud remains an accepted alias.

Variable Default Description OPENAI_API_KEY Required for openai-compatible API key used by the OpenAI-compatible client. OPENAI_BASE_URL https://api.openai.com/v1 OpenAI-compatible endpoint. OPENAI_MODEL gpt-5-mini Default model used by the agents.

For Ollama Cloud, set:

AWARE_LLM_PROVIDER=ollama
OLLAMA_API_KEY=your_ollama_cloud_api_key
OLLAMA_MODEL=gemma4:31b

OLLAMA_BASE_URL defaults to https://ollama.com/v1, and OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS defaults to 120. Use a model available in your Ollama Cloud account. The --llm-model CLI option takes precedence over OLLAMA_MODEL; the UI uses OLLAMA_MODEL. With the OpenAI-compatible provider, --llm-model similarly overrides OPENAI_MODEL. The active model is resolved from the selected provider at the start of each run.

The Ollama Cloud adapter includes the expected JSON schema in the prompt instead of sending a response_format parameter. Aware checks returned JSON in the Parser and Executor and retries invalid Parser results. An Executor response that cannot be parsed falls back to its existing heuristic path. An API key is required; keep it in .env or the process environment, not in a command argument.

docs.title: Parser and Executor
docs.text:
Variable Default Description PARSER_MAX_ATTEMPTS 5 Maximum parser repair attempts. EXECUTOR_MAX_AGENTS 5 Maximum total Executor sub-agents created per incident analysis, including initial domain agents, V3 specialists, and focused follow-ups. The value is displayed in the UI. EXECUTOR_MAX_EXPANSIONS 2 Maximum focused follow-up agents after the initial domain coverage; clamped to 0–4. AWARE_PARSER_KB_FILE knowledge/parser_buildspec_kb.md Parser knowledge file path. AWARE_EXECUTOR_V3_KB_FILE knowledge/executor_rca_v3_kb.md V3 mechanism-oriented technical knowledge.

Seed analysis is demand-driven: metrics run first, followed by logs and traces, then independent V3 metric experts when metrics are available. The safety limit is a ceiling, not a target agent count. Each batch incident gets its own SQLite database by default when memory is enabled.

docs.title: Runtime Toggles
docs.text:
Variable Default Description AWARE_ENABLE_REASONING true Enables richer reasoning prompts. AWARE_ENABLE_MEMORY true Enables shared memory and SQLite writes.

When AWARE_ENABLE_REASONING=false, the LLM is still used, but prompts are more direct.

When AWARE_ENABLE_MEMORY=false, inter-agent memory and SQLite writes are disabled.

docs.title: Knowledge DB
docs.text:
Default database file path (one file per run):

output/memory/run-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-xxxxxxxx.db

The timestamp is UTC and the suffix prevents collisions when runs start in the same second. CLI and UI batch incidents each receive a separate database under output/batches/<batch-id>/memory/. AWARE resolves the path to an absolute SQLite URL, which is included in the run's event stream and artifacts. The default database is created when analysis starts; the UI does not restore a previously saved database URL.

Override it from the CLI:

aware assess \
  --query "checkout timeout" \
  --repo /path/to/repository \
  --db-url sqlite:///output/custom-assess.db

An explicit CLI URL intentionally reuses that database and may put it outside the batch directory. UI API callers can also pass an explicit db_url request parameter; the browser UI uses a fresh database for each run.

docs.title: Batch CLI parameters
docs.text:
aware batch accepts --dataset (nezha, openrca_bank, openrca_market, or openrca_telecom) and --source for an extracted dataset. --limit selects the number of incidents; --max-agents, --max-attempts, and --llm-model override the corresponding runtime values for that command. --batch-id, --results-csv, --graph-dir, --db-url, and --json control naming, output locations, and the printed summary. Omitting the output overrides keeps the generated files together in one timestamped batch directory. See Usage.

The UI refreshes the configured provider and model from .env while it is open. Values explicitly exported in the server's shell still take precedence.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or newer
  • An OpenAI-compatible API endpoint and key, or an Ollama Cloud account and API key
  • An extracted Nezha or OpenRCA dataset with its incident labels and telemetry

The raw datasets are excluded from Git. Download and extract the dataset you want to analyze before running a batch. A ZIP file alone is not a valid --source for execution.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Create a virtual environment and install AWARE:

python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .

Install the test and documentation dependencies only when needed:

pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"

docs.title: Choose an LLM provider
docs.text:
Copy the configuration template:

cp .env.example .env

For an OpenAI-compatible API, set AWARE_LLM_PROVIDER=openai-compatible, OPENAI_API_KEY, and OPENAI_MODEL. For Ollama Cloud, set AWARE_LLM_PROVIDER=ollama, OLLAMA_API_KEY, and OLLAMA_MODEL. The ollama provider name selects Ollama Cloud. See Configuration for the endpoint and runtime settings. Keep actual keys in .env or your shell; .env is ignored by Git.

docs.title: Run a dataset batch
docs.text:
Analyze the first five incidents from an extracted Nezha dataset:

aware batch --dataset nezha --source /path/to/extracted/Nezha --limit 5

OpenRCA uses the same command structure. For example:

aware batch --dataset openrca_bank --source /path/to/extracted/Bank-003 --limit 5

Use openrca_market or openrca_telecom for the other OpenRCA datasets. --source may also point to a telemetry folder inside an extracted dataset. AWARE prepares the incident requests from the catalogue, so a batch does not need --query or a manually prepared CSV. --max-agents 5 can override the per-incident agent ceiling from .env.

At startup, the CLI reports the provider, model, reasoning and memory settings, incident count, and agent limit. It writes a timestamped directory under output/batches/ containing the selected catalogue, scores, reports, graphs, journals, and one SQLite memory file per incident when memory is enabled.

For the browser interface, run aware ui --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8787 and open http://127.0.0.1:8787. See Web UI for its batch workflow.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Each successful or failed run can produce local artifacts and optional SQLite records.

docs.title: Artifact Files
docs.text:
Standalone runs are saved automatically under:

output/json/<timestamp>_<run_id>.json
output/txt/<timestamp>_<run_id>.txt

The JSON artifact contains structured parser, executor, and assessment data. The text artifact is a human-readable report.

docs.title: Batch Results
docs.text:
aware batch prints its UTC timestamped batch ID and output directory. Browser batches also use a timestamped ID. By default, both interfaces group batch files under output/batches/<batch-id>/:

  • results.csv: one row per incident, with the predicted cause, score, agent count, and artifact paths.
  • config.json: provider, model, reasoning and memory flags, agent limit, and input locations; no API keys.
  • problems.csv: snapshot of the incidents selected for this batch.
  • manifest.json: incident IDs, run IDs, statuses, and journal paths.
  • incidents/<problem-id>.json and .log: complete event journals and results.
  • json/ and txt/: per-incident structured and readable reports.
  • graphs/<problem-id>-causal-graph.png: graph image when a graph was produced.
  • memory/<run-id>.db: one SQLite database per incident when memory is enabled.

CLI IDs use batch-cli-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-xxxxxx; UI IDs use the same UTC timestamp format with the batch-ui- prefix. T separates date and time, and Z indicates UTC. Existing batch directories keep their original names.

The results.csv file records each incident's predicted and expected cause, component/reason/time checks, overall score, agent count, and artifact paths. It includes the memory database path when memory is enabled. The CLI PNG and UI graph identify the selected component, cause, occurrence time in the incident's configured timezone, and confidence. Observations without a displayed graph relation appear in a separate Other findings area beneath the causal chain. Explicit output path overrides may place selected files outside this directory.

docs.title: Assessment Sections
docs.text:
The final assessment output can include:

Section Description buildspec_resolution_scope How the BuildSpec scope was resolved. root_cause_synthesis Cross-domain synthesis from logs, traces, and metrics. findings Structured findings reported by executor sub-agents. anomalies Anomalies detected during telemetry analysis. preliminary_causes Candidate causes inferred from the executor output. final_reporting Final report fields requested by the BuildSpec.

docs.title: SQLite Knowledge DB
docs.text:
When memory is enabled, Aware writes runtime information to SQLite.

Default file path for a standalone run:

output/memory/run-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-xxxxxxxx.db

For either CLI or browser batches, the default file path is output/batches/<batch-id>/memory/<run-id>.db. AWARE logs the resolved absolute SQLite URL for the run. No memory database is created when AWARE_ENABLE_MEMORY=false.

Tables:

  • runs
  • events
  • task_results
  • findings
  • component_memory

This database is useful for later inspection, debugging, and comparing assessment runs.

docs.title: Web UI
docs.text: The web UI provides a live view of the Parser and Executor runtime. It is useful when you want to inspect agent events, generated BuildSpecs, findings, anomalies, and root-cause synthesis without reading raw artifacts.

docs.title: Start the UI
docs.text:
aware ui --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8787

Open:

http://127.0.0.1:8787

The UI always runs the V3 strategy. V3 keeps the initial opinions independent, adds conservative JVM, MySQL, and Redis metric experts, reconciles their evidence after analysis, and emits an inspectable causal graph. The graph separates raw evidence, observed components, candidate hypotheses, contradictions, and the selected outcome.

docs.title: Main Inputs
docs.text:
Field Description Run mode Dataset batch prepares and runs catalogue incidents; Single problem runs one manually entered incident question. Dataset Select Nezha, OpenRCA · Bank, OpenRCA · Market, or OpenRCA · Telecom to activate the corresponding paths, timezone, catalogue, and telemetry layout. Telemetry directory Path to the extracted dataset or one of its telemetry folders. For a batch, the backend finds the incident labels higher in that dataset and uses the right source directory for each incident. Incident question Required only in Single problem mode. Include the date and start/end of the failure interval. Dataset batches generate this question from the catalogue.

The incident timezone is selected automatically from the dataset profile (Nezha uses UTC; OpenRCA and Generic default to UTC+08:00). The UI displays the EXECUTOR_MAX_AGENTS limit from .env beneath Model, Reasoning, and Memory. This is the total number of Executor agents that may be created for one incident, including initial domain agents, V3 specialists, and focused follow-ups; it is not a concurrency limit. The default is 5. Each incident in a batch has its own limit. Each run uses a separate SQLite memory file; the memory database control is hidden in the UI.

docs.title: Runtime Panels
docs.text:
• Dashboard opens first. It shows the selected dataset, mode and telemetry directory, background incident preparation, batch progress, run metrics, the latest diagnosis and recent agent activity. Result and event links appear when those outputs exist.
  • The configuration sidebar keeps the launch controls and runtime status together. On smaller screens, the dashboard appears first with a link to the configuration form; launching returns to the dashboard.
  • Assessment summary surfaces the component, reason, occurrence time, and confidence.
  • Live analysis shows streamed events and the latest state of each agent for both single incidents and batches.
  • Findings presents evidence and anomalies as readable cards.
  • Causal graph shows the selected component, cause, time, and confidence above the diagram and inside the outcome node when a diagnosis is available. Evidence, components, hypotheses, and the outcome are grouped in related rows. Unlinked observations appear in a separate, shaded Other findings section below the causal chain; their horizontal position does not imply a relation to a component or hypothesis. Select a node by mouse or keyboard to highlight its direct relations and read its full label and provenance. The graph fits the available width on desktop; small screens keep readable text with horizontal scrolling. Export SVG saves a scalable vector image. Export PNG saves the complete graph at up to 4× resolution, capped at 24 megapixels, with a white background, regardless of the current zoom or selection.
  • Technical data keeps the BuildSpec, scope, synthesis, and final JSON available for inspection.
  • Run metrics show elapsed time, event count, finding count, the exact number of ephemeral agents created, and execution state.

The dataset and source path are retained locally in the browser. Live monitoring can be disconnected; this closes the browser stream but does not cancel an assessment already running on the server.

docs.title: Nezha example
docs.text:
Select Nezha. The UI switches the timezone to UTC, uses the configured agent limit, uses the locally extracted example when available, and inserts this question:

On January 30, 2023, between 11:50:30 and 11:53:30 UTC, one failure occurred. Identify the root cause component, occurrence time, and reason.

The interval must contain UTC clock times as stored by Nezha. No manual conversion to UTC+08 is needed. The final occurrence timestamp is displayed as a readable date and time in the selected timezone.

docs.title: Nezha dataset batch
docs.text:
The UI supports both Single problem and Dataset batch run modes. To assess the complete dataset:

  1. Select Nezha and Dataset batch.
  2. Enter the extracted dataset directory or a telemetry folder inside it. The backend finds the official *-fault_list.json files and the UI shows the incident count when ready.
  3. Leave Problem limit blank to run all incidents, or enter a smaller number for a smoke test.
  4. Click Analyze batch. If preparation is still running, the click waits for it and then starts the batch.

There is no problems CSV download or upload step in the UI. The backend returns the prepared incidents directly and the browser reuses that list when the batch starts.

Problems run sequentially. Once the backend prepares the incidents, the full queue is visible with a PENDING status. During execution, exactly one row changes to RUNNING; completed rows become PASS, FAIL, or ERROR. The Agents column reports how many ephemeral agents were created for each incident. The Graph column opens the causal graph for that row. The graph view also provides an incident selector, so completing a later assessment does not remove access to earlier graphs in the same batch. The browser also shows progress, overall success rate, and separate component, reason, and time rates. Export results CSV downloads the detailed predictions, agent counts, scores, run IDs, and log links after at least one problem completes.

If execution fails, the incident row shows ERROR and the error message. The live event feed remains available during a batch, so a run that is still working is distinguishable from one that failed to start. The batch control is labelled Stop batch; it stops the browser queue while an assessment already started on the server may continue.

Every browser batch receives a UTC timestamped ID such as batch-ui-20261112T143015Z-a1b2c3. Before analysis, the backend saves the selected incidents and runtime configuration. Each incident then writes its memory, reports, graph, result row, and complete journals inside that batch directory, even if the browser connection closes:

output/batches/<batch_id>/
├── config.json
├── problems.csv
├── results.csv
├── manifest.json
├── incidents/<problem_id>.json and .log
├── json/ and txt/
├── graphs/<problem_id>-causal-graph.png
└── memory/<run_id>.db

The graph file is written when a causal graph exists, and the SQLite file when memory is enabled. An explicit database URL supplied by an API caller can place memory outside the batch directory; the browser uses the per-run default. The JSON journal contains the run ID, status, exact agent count, every emitted runtime event, artifact paths, error details, the causal graph when produced, and the complete result payload. The batch table exposes JSON and TXT links per incident, while Backend batch log opens the manifest for the whole batch.

Each prepared incident contains:

problem_id,system,date,start_time,end_time,timezone_offset_minutes,source_path,expected_component,expected_time,expected_reason

The generated catalogue contains 56 OnlineBoutique incidents and 45 TrainTicket incidents. Each row is a simple incident, not a Parser task. The UI constructs the standard diagnostic question from its date and UTC interval. Ground-truth columns are only used by the browser to score a completed diagnosis; they are not sent to ParserAgent or ExecutorAgent.

Scoring is deliberately strict and reproducible:

  • component: exact pod-name match;
  • reason: normalized match, so network_delay and network delay are equivalent;
  • occurrence time: predicted UNIX timestamp within 60 seconds of the label;
  • overall success: all three checks pass.

docs.title: Adaptive agent lifecycle
docs.text:
Nezha uses the configured runtime agent limit. ExecutorAgent creates at most one seed agent per available domain, in the order metrics, logs, then traces. All selected files in a domain are consolidated into one context and one LLM decision, so neither the number of files nor the number of CSV shards multiplies the number of agents or model calls. Each ephemeral agent reads shared memory, analyzes its assigned evidence need, writes its result and findings to SQLite, and terminates.

After each useful seed result, strict convergence rules may cancel domains that can no longer change the result: one unique long-form KPI anomaly can stop after metrics, and one repeated local return/exception can stop after logs. Propagated caller errors and competing hypotheses never trigger this shortcut. Otherwise a cross-domain synthesis checkpoint runs after normal coverage. A medium/low-confidence result, any unresolved field, or an explicit coordinator verification request can create a component-focused follow-up even when a provisional component has already been named. Requested domains may revisit the same files with this narrower focus. There are at most two follow-ups and no recursive expansion, so the normal range is one to three seed agents and five remains the default hard adaptive maximum.

Canonical dataset incidents for Nezha and OpenRCA use a deterministic, validated Parser fast path. Free-form questions still use the retrying Parser LLM. OpenRCA catalogues join the official observation windows from query.csv with the component, timestamp, and reason ground truth from record.csv; a window is split at midpoints only when it contains multiple labelled incidents.

The root-cause reason list in executor knowledge is a non-exhaustive candidate vocabulary. Agents may add a telemetry-backed novel cause; absence from the initial list does not invalidate it.

docs.title: OpenRCA Bank, Market, and Telecom
docs.text:
The three OpenRCA datasets use local datetimes in UTC+08:00. Their record.csv timestamps are converted consistently with that offset; do not select UTC for these catalogues.

Select the desired OpenRCA dataset, Dataset batch, and its telemetry directory. The backend prepares the catalogue automatically and populates the incident queue. Each catalogue contains one simple full-RCA incident per ground-truth record:

The CLI uses the same dataset preparation with aware batch --dataset openrca_bank --source /path/to/extracted/Bank-003 --limit 5 (or openrca_market / openrca_telecom). The --source directory must be extracted before analysis.

Dataset Problems Systems Bank 136 bank Market 148 cloudbed-1 and cloudbed-2 Telecom 51 telecom

Each problem asks for component, occurrence time, and reason using the official interval parsed from query.csv. This avoids converting the benchmark's partial task_1–task_7 questions into UI tasks. When an official query interval contains several labelled failures, it is divided at the midpoint between consecutive record.csv occurrences so that every UI row remains a single incident. Market rows automatically point to the correct cloudbed directory.

OpenRCA file selection is deterministic: only telemetry files below the incident's YYYY_MM_DD directory are passed to ExecutorAgent. A telemetry family may be explicitly empty when it does not exist. In particular, Telecom contains traces and metrics but no log files, so its BuildSpec uses absolute_log_file: [] instead of inventing a path or rejecting the incident.

Agent counts, per-incident JSON/TXT journals, the batch manifest, scoring, and results CSV work exactly as described for Nezha. The dataset profile is also inferred from each problem ID during a batch, preventing an accidentally selected UI profile from applying Nezha rules to an OpenRCA CSV.

docs.title: Typical Flow
docs.text:
1. Select the dataset profile.
  2. Enter the telemetry directory and incident query.
  3. Click Analyze incident.
  4. Watch Parser validation and Executor analysis events.
  5. Review the final JSON sections in the result panels.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Aware exposes a CLI through the aware command. Use aware batch for a Nezha or OpenRCA dataset: it generates incident requests from the catalogue, so you provide a dataset path and options instead of writing a --query. Use aware assess when you have a single, free-form incident question.

docs.title: Run a Dataset Batch
docs.text:
One command prepares the incident catalogue and analyzes the first five incidents for any supported dataset:

aware batch --dataset nezha --source /path/to/extracted/Nezha --limit 5
aware batch --dataset openrca_bank --source /path/to/extracted/Bank-003 --limit 5
aware batch --dataset openrca_market --source /path/to/extracted/Market-002 --limit 5
aware batch --dataset openrca_telecom --source /path/to/extracted/Telecom-001 --limit 5

The values for --dataset match the UI's dataset profiles. Market and Telecom must be extracted before use; an archive path alone cannot supply telemetry to the Executor. The raw datasets are ignored by Git.

--source points to an extracted dataset directory or a telemetry folder inside it. The CLI locates the catalogue above that folder, as the UI does. --limit counts incidents; the EXECUTOR_MAX_AGENTS value from .env limits agents created for each incident. AWARE saves the exact selected catalogue as problems.csv in the batch output directory. OpenRCA uses the same --dataset, --source, and --limit options as Nezha; no manual --query or CSV preparation is needed.

For an explicit run configuration, the same command can include the parser retry limit, agent ceiling, and model override:

aware batch \
  --dataset openrca_bank \
  --source /path/to/extracted/Bank-003 \
  --limit 5 \
  --max-agents 5 \
  --max-attempts 5 \
  --llm-model MODEL_AVAILABLE_ON_YOUR_PROVIDER

The provider, its API key, reasoning, and memory are configured in .env or the process environment. --llm-model overrides the model for the selected provider. --max-agents is a total ceiling per incident, not a batch-wide count or concurrency setting. Without an override, EXECUTOR_MAX_AGENTS in .env applies.

docs.title: Run an Existing Problems CSV Batch
docs.text:
Run an AWARE problems CSV using the same timestamped batch directory:

aware batch \
  --problems-csv /path/to/problems.csv \
  --limit 5 \
  --max-agents 8

Omit --limit 5 to run every CSV incident. Each row may provide its own source_path; otherwise pass --repo as a fallback. Expected component, time, and reason columns are used only after execution for scoring and are never sent to ParserAgent or ExecutorAgent.

The command writes:

  • output/batches/<batch-id>/results.csv with component, reason, time, and overall scores;
  • output/batches/<batch-id>/config.json with the provider, model, reasoning, memory, and agent limit used;
  • output/batches/<batch-id>/problems.csv with the exact selected incidents, including CSV input batches;
  • output/batches/<batch-id>/json/ and txt/ with one report per incident;
  • output/batches/<batch-id>/manifest.json and per-incident journals in incidents/;
  • causal-graph PNGs in graphs/ when the graphs are non-empty;
  • one SQLite file per incident in memory/ when memory is enabled.

At startup the CLI prints the provider, model, reasoning, memory, incident count, and agent limit. At completion it prints the batch ID and output directory. The default ID is batch-cli-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-xxxxxx, using UTC just like the UI's batch-ui- IDs. A custom --batch-id replaces the generated ID. Explicit --db-url, --results-csv, and --graph-dir paths still take precedence and may place those files outside the batch directory.

docs.title: Run the Full Assessment
docs.text:
Use assess for the full Parser + Executor workflow.

aware assess \
  --query "On 2021-03-04 between 18:30:00 and 19:00:00 checkout timeout" \
  --repo /path/to/repository

docs.title: Parse a Request
docs.text:
Use parse when you only want to generate and validate a BuildSpec.

aware parse \
  --query "On 2021-03-04 between 18:30:00 and 19:00:00 checkout timeout" \
  --repo /path/to/repository

docs.title: Execute an Existing BuildSpec
docs.text:
Use execute when a BuildSpec already exists and you want to run the executor stage.

aware execute \
  --buildspec-json /path/to/buildspec.json \
  --repo /path/to/repository

docs.title: Useful Options
docs.text: Option Scope Description --source (--repo) Batch Extracted dataset directory, an internal telemetry directory, or fallback telemetry directory for a CSV. --repo Parse / Execute / Assess Telemetry repository for one incident. --query Parser / Assess Natural-language incident request. --buildspec-json Execute Path to an existing BuildSpec JSON file. --problems-csv Batch AWARE problems catalogue to execute. --dataset Batch Build a catalogue directly from nezha, openrca_bank, openrca_market, or openrca_telecom. --limit Batch Number of incidents to analyze. --max-attempts Parse / Assess / Batch Maximum Parser retry attempts; overrides PARSER_MAX_ATTEMPTS. --batch-id Batch Custom batch directory ID; otherwise a UTC timestamped ID is generated. --results-csv Batch Results and scoring CSV destination. --graph-dir Batch V3 causal graph PNG directory. --db-url Execute / Assess / Batch SQLite database URL override. --max-agents Execute / Assess / Batch Maximum number of executor sub-agents per incident. --llm-model Parser / Assess / Batch LLM model override. --json CLI JSON output; for batch, prints the final summary as JSON.

docs.title: BuildSpec Multiple Files
docs.text:
The BuildSpec supports multiple files per telemetry domain:

  • absolute_log_file: list of absolute log paths
  • absolute_trace_file: list of absolute trace paths
  • absolute_metrics_file: list of absolute metrics paths
